summary: Solid hardening over the expiring test-mode rules: the database is no longer wide open, writes are confined to five validated paths with strict field/type/size checks, and privilege escalation is impossible because room membership is server-only. However, the app never signs the browser in to Firebase Auth (auth is Clerk + Liveblocks), so rules cannot verify WHO a caller is. Every document is publicly readable and document title/tags/versions/chat-message creation is open to anyone with the public API key, and room membership (emails) is exposed through the collection-group queries. This is the deliberate, documented trade-off of an identity-less ruleset; the Clerk-to-Firebase-Auth custom-token bridge is the real fix.

findings.issue: No identity check is possible: request.auth is always null because the client never signs in to Firebase Auth. Anyone with the public API key can read any document, edit any document's title/tags, create version snapshots or chat messages with a spoofed userId, and delete version snapshots.
findings.recommendation: Bridge Clerk to Firebase Auth (server action mints admin.createCustomToken(email), client calls signInWithCustomToken once on boot), then replace `read: if true` with membership checks against users/{email}/rooms/{roomId} and validate the caller's uid on writes. Documented at the bottom of firestore.rules as NEXT STEP.

findings.issue: Collection-group queries on `rooms` (useOwner's roomId filter and the dashboard search's userId filter) cannot be scoped to the caller without identity, so `users/{email}/rooms/{roomId}` is publicly readable — that leaks room membership, i.e. member emails.
findings.recommendation: With the auth bridge: scope the read to resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid and add where('userId','==', myEmail) to useOwner's query so it stays legal.

findings.issue: Version snapshots are capped at 1,000,000 chars per snapshot (the app's own autosnapshot design) but there is no per-document or per-caller rate limit, so a visitor can spam version documents. Tags array elements are not type-checked (rules cannot iterate list elements).
findings.recommendation: With the auth bridge, gate version creation on room membership; consider moving version pruning server-side (it already exists as a server action in versionHistory.ts).

findings.issue: Not exploitable: users/{email}/rooms/{roomId} is read-only to the browser and roles ('owner') are written only by server actions, so no caller can grant itself a role or write to another user's membership tree.
findings.recommendation: Keep membership writes server-only when the auth bridge lands.

findings.issue: Verified consistent: documents are create/delete-denied and updates restricted to validated title/tags; versions are create-validated, update-denied; chat messages are create-validated, update/delete-denied; comments are entirely server-managed.
